title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is designed to protect democratic processes by preventing and mitigating the spread of AI‑generated misinformation that could influence voters. It establishes legal standards and enforcement mechanisms for election officials and technology providers to detect, disclose, and counter AI‑driven deceptive content during campaign periods.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are about to collapse because of stress in the AI market. Instead, Congress should focus on providing aid to all Americans who have been harmed.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets rules for AI research to make sure systems are trustworthy, transparent, and safe for society. It requires researchers to follow strict testing, documentation, and public disclosure standards, and creates oversight to prevent harmful or unreliable AI from being deployed.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law that requires the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to clearly explain when and how artificial intelligence is used in its services. It mandates that veterans and regulators can see the data, algorithms, and decision‑making processes behind AI tools to ensure they are fair, safe, and accountable.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to make the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ claims transparent, reliable, and fair. It establishes oversight, audit requirements, and safeguards to protect veterans’ rights while promoting efficient and accurate claims handling.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act is designed to safeguard consumers from being misled by false or deceptive claims about AI technologies. It requires companies to clearly disclose when AI is used, how it functions, and ensures accurate representation of the AI's capabilities and limitations.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law that requires companies and developers to identify, test, and mitigate security risks in powerful AI systems. It also establishes oversight and accountability measures to ensure AI technologies are built and deployed with robust safeguards that protect public safety.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to develop and implement measures that protect artificial intelligence systems from cyber threats. The act aims to coordinate federal resources, expertise, and partnerships to enhance the security, resilience, and trustworthiness of AI technologies across the nation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 aims to set up clear rules for evaluating, reducing, and monitoring the dangers posed by AI systems, making sure they operate safely and securely. It requires companies to be transparent and accountable, report problems, and protect personal data while giving regulators the tools to enforce these standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to create a national framework for the safe deployment and integration of autonomous AI-powered machines in everyday life. It establishes oversight mechanisms, standards for interoperability, and coordination between federal agencies to ensure these systems operate reliably and without unintended harm.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that aims to safeguard electoral integrity by regulating the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigning and election-related communications. It seeks to prevent manipulation or misinformation generated by AI tools that could influence voter behavior or distort the democratic process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act aims to regulate artificial intelligence systems that can learn and adapt on their own. It establishes monitoring protocols, reporting requirements, and oversight mechanisms to ensure these systems remain safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to halt the creation and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that pose significant risks to public safety, privacy, and society at large. It calls for strict regulations, oversight, and accountability measures to prevent AI from operating without adequate safety protocols and ethical safeguards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on building new data centers specifically for artificial intelligence use, aiming to assess environmental, economic, and social impacts before further expansion. It sets a temporary halt to new AI data center construction, allowing time for studies and stakeholder input on the long‑term effects of large-scale AI infrastructure.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act creates a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to examine incidents involving AI systems and their impact on national security. The board will investigate threats, recommend safeguards, and help ensure AI technologies are used safely and responsibly.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is designed to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence in the United States so that it serves the interests of American citizens. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and equitable access to AI benefits while protecting privacy and preventing discrimination.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and research labs in China to submit regular reports on their artificial‑intelligence projects, covering development progress, usage data and any potential national‑security risks. This reporting is intended to give regulators better visibility into AI capabilities, promote transparency, and help shape policy around the growth and safe deployment of AI technology.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law designed to keep humans at the center of medical care, limiting the use of artificial intelligence in diagnosing, treating, and managing patients. It sets rules and safeguards to prevent AI from replacing qualified doctors, thereby protecting patient safety and professional accountability.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President. This office would monitor, assess, and mitigate risks posed by AI and other emerging technologies.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI policy, regulation, and oversight. It aims to coordinate government efforts, set guidelines, and ensure AI development aligns with national interests and values.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 mandates that companies conduct formal risk assessments of their AI systems before they are released or used in public settings. It aims to identify potential harms—such as bias, privacy breaches, or safety issues—and require mitigation plans, reporting, and oversight to ensure AI technologies operate responsibly and transparently.
